newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bosnian Croats abolish separatist republic.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Croats abolish separatist republic.

text.p: Bosnian Croats said on Thursday their separatist Herceg-Bosna state in the south had formally ceased to exist, giving a boost to the fragile Moslem-Croat federation occupying half of the country.
The Croatian news agency HINA reported that Federation president Kresimir Zubak, a Croat, told Western mediatiors "the government and the ministries of Herceg-Bosna have stopped functioning".
The Bosnian Croat leadership issued a statement saying the transfer of power from Herceg-Bosnian institutions to those of the Moslem-Croat federation had been completed.
Bosnian Croats formed Herceg-Bosna with support from Zagreb in late 1992, after war broke out between Serbs, Croats and Moslems.
The following year Moslems and Croats, who had been allied against the Serbs, fell out and fought for land in central and southern Bosnia.
The two communities made peace in January 1994 under U.S. pressure and agreed to form a bi-national federation.
The Dayton peace treaty signed at the end of 1995 envisaged a Bosnia divided between the Serb republic and the Moslem-Croat federation.
But Herceg-Bosna, with its distinctly Croat institutions, insignia, money and police continued to exist, defying Western demands for total commitment to the federation.
The Croats countered by accusing their Moslem partners of foot-dragging in dissolving the institutions of the pre-war Moslem Bosnian republic.
Western mediators had expressed concern that the continued existance of a Croat mini-state would tear apart the joint federation and spark a renewed ethnic conflict.

"(The Bosnian Croat leadership) will make further efforts to continue the positive trend of strengthening mutual trust and of setting up the functioning federal authorities," the Bosnian wing of the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) said on Thursday.
HDZ said it would nominate ex-defence minister Vladimir Soljic, a Croat, for the post of Federation president.
